article_title: Let a hundred flowers bloom; let a hundred schools of thought contend
citation: Gerry Stahl & Friedrich Hesse. (2011). Let a hundred flowers bloom; let a hundred schools of thought contend. Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning, 6, 139-145. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-011-9118-8
title: Hong Kong Knowledge-Building Teachers Network (KBTN): a network connecting policy, teacher peer support, research, theory and technology
description: KBTN is a teacher network in Hong Kong, funded continuously since 2006 by the Hong Kong Ministry of Education in line with reforms going back to 2000, and based on Scardamalia and Bereiter's knowledge-building theory and the Knowledge Forum environment. The editorial describes it as "a meeting place of forward-looking government policy initiatives, teacher peer support, CSCL researcher initiative, well-established CSCL theory, and the use of CSCL technology." Chan analyzes it at macro, meso, and micro levels of transformation from an action researcher's perspective.
requirements: Sustained funding and alignment with government educational reform policy
constraints: Chan refrains from final evaluation or recommendation, recognizing the effort is ongoing and its lessons must be resituated in other settings
target_learners: Hong Kong teachers adopting knowledge-building pedagogy
target_learning_goals: Connecting CSCL insights to local educational policy and classroom practice
examples: In Hong Kong the impetus was driven more by researchers and teachers and a relatively mature technology was introduced, whereas in Singapore the government led and technology design was still evolving
key_sources: Gerry Stahl & Friedrich Hesse. (2011). Let a hundred flowers bloom; let a hundred schools of thought contend. Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning, 6, 139-145. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-011-9118-8

article_title: Collaborative analytics-supported reflective Assessment for Scaffolding Pre-service Teachers’ collaborative Inquiry and Knowledge Building
citation: Yang, Y., Zhu, G., Sun, D., & Chan, C. K. K. (2022). Collaborative analytics-supported reflective Assessment for Scaffolding Pre-service Teachers’ collaborative Inquiry and Knowledge Building. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-022-09372-y
title: KBDeX (Knowledge Building Discourse Explorer) social network analysis tool used to visualize collaborative ideas and discourse for student reflection
description: KBDeX is "a social network analysis tool designed to visualize and represent collaborative ideas and discourse" (Oshima et al., 2012). Its primary purpose is "to analyze online discourse data to depict community advances", and it is used mostly by researchers; in this study the authors developed KBDeX output as visualization diagrams that students used as feedback on their ongoing Knowledge Forum discussions. Visualizations included growth curves of the cumulative degree centrality of ideas and idea network maps, which PSTs were taught to read and use for reflection and assessment of their discourse.
requirements: Instructor guidance on key social network analysis terms (e.g., density, degree centrality) and on how to read the visualizations and data before student use
constraints: KBDeX is used mostly by researchers; this study adapted its output into student-facing diagrams rather than using the tool as originally intended
target_learners: pre-service teachers in an 18-week university course
target_learning_goals: monitoring and assessing collective knowledge building discourse
identifying promising routes for further inquiry
examples: The instructor ran KBDeX, explained key terms and parameters, and facilitated whole-class discussion of how to interpret the growth curve of cumulative degree centrality and the idea network map
key_sources: Yang, Y., Zhu, G., Sun, D., & Chan, C. K. K. (2022). Collaborative analytics-supported reflective Assessment for Scaffolding Pre-service Teachers’ collaborative Inquiry and Knowledge Building. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-022-09372-y

article_title: Knowledge building–modeling: Grade 5 students creating models, using discourse analytics, and advancing systems thinking
citation: Dina Soliman, Xueqi Feng, Marlene Scardamalia, Carol Chan. (2026). Knowledge building–modeling: Grade 5 students creating models, using discourse analytics, and advancing systems thinking. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-026-09493-8
title: Knowledge Building–Modeling (KBM): a recursive framework integrating discourse, analytics-driven reflection, and model construction
description: KBM is a proposed framework with three constructs—discourse, analytics-supported reflection, and modeling—in which 'scientific modeling is integrated within the flow of discourse and guided by knowledge building analytics to support systems thinking and knowledge advances'. Discourse informs model construction; models serve as provocations for continued discourse; analytics visualizations support meta-reflection and planning. Models function as boundary objects and improvable artifacts positioned as public goods within the knowledge building community.
requirements: Students need to engage in both collaborative discourse and ongoing modeling and reorganization of their evolving knowledge landscape
Knowledge Forum as a collaborative discourse space, Idea-Friend Map visualizations, and model-construction mediums as design embodiments
constraints: The article states that arrows in the conjecture map represent dynamic relationships 'not reducible to distinct pathways'—the constructs jointly co-mediate one another
target_learning_goals: epistemic agency and collective knowledge advancement
examples: The 9-session Earth Science and Systems Thinking unit organized into three phases: introducing systems thinking, Idea-Friend Map-guided model reconstruction, and epistemic-marker-supported model-based reasoning
key_sources: Dina Soliman, Xueqi Feng, Marlene Scardamalia, Carol Chan. (2026). Knowledge building–modeling: Grade 5 students creating models, using discourse analytics, and advancing systems thinking. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-026-09493-8

article_title: Why Growth Mindset Training Alone may not Improve Academic Outcomes: A Call for Research on Bundling Growth Mindset and Retrieval Practice Interventions
citation: Anne M. Cleary, Daniel H. Robinson. (2026). Why Growth Mindset Training Alone may not Improve Academic Outcomes: A Call for Research on Bundling Growth Mindset and Retrieval Practice Interventions. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10188-7
title: KBCP framework: knowledge, belief, commitment, and planning as sequential requirements for students' adoption of study strategies
description: The review describes the knowledge, belief, commitment, and planning (KBCP) framework of McDaniel et al. (2021), which "holds that students must first have the knowledge that a particular study strategy will work, believe that it will work, commit to using it, and then make a plan for using it." The article positions GMT within this framework as potentially serving the purpose of instilling a belief that learning can be improved with adherence to the right strategies, making it a stepping-stone rather than a standalone treatment.
requirements: Students must first have knowledge that a study strategy will work, then believe it, commit to using it, and plan for using it
constraints: The review notes more research is needed to further explore the suggestion of combining science of learning and socio-motivational interventions
target_learners: college students trained in learning strategies in the cited pilot course context
K-12 and higher education students targeted by study-strategy interventions
target_learning_goals: adoption and persistent use of effective, science-backed learning strategies such as retrieval practice and spacing
examples: The article proposes that within the KBCP framework, GMT could serve the purpose of instilling a belief that learning can be improved with adherence to the right strategies
key_sources: Anne M. Cleary, Daniel H. Robinson. (2026). Why Growth Mindset Training Alone may not Improve Academic Outcomes: A Call for Research on Bundling Growth Mindset and Retrieval Practice Interventions. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10188-7

article_title: Triggers of curiosity in social constructivist classroom discourse
citation: Ali, F., Wang, Y., Wang, S. J.-W. & Zhu, G. (2025). Triggers of curiosity in social constructivist classroom discourse. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00330-5
title: Knowledge Building as a social constructivist pedagogical model provides the discourse context in which curiosity chains emerge
description: Knowledge Building (KB) is the pedagogical model underpinning the studied classrooms: it is "underpinned by social constructivism," emphasizing "inquiry and dialog-based classroom discourse" and "collaborative engagement and knowledge creation as a learning community." A distinguishing characteristic is "students’shared responsibility for learning and propelling the discourse forward," with teachers facilitating rather than leading. The article treats KB discourse as the ideal context in which antecedents, triggers, and manifestations of curiosity can be examined.
requirements: Discourse serves as the mediator, with students constructing and expressing knowledge through dialogue
constraints: The study's curiosity findings are limited to social constructivist classrooms implementing KB; I-R-E style conventional classrooms differ in utterance types and quality
target_learners: elementary students in student-centered, inquiry-based classrooms
target_learning_goals: collaborative knowledge creation and community knowledge building through dialogue
examples: Ten-month KB courses were conducted in second grade (topic: growth and changes in animals, Atlantic salmon) and third grade (topic: soil in the environment), with books, artifacts, visiting experts, and field visits.
key_sources: Ali, F., Wang, Y., Wang, S. J.-W. & Zhu, G. (2025). Triggers of curiosity in social constructivist classroom discourse. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00330-5
